I'm not sure, since I never use the fortify functions in that way (since getting the order right is such a touchy business). I usually go through the object (e.g., SpatialPolygonsDataFrame) directly with a for loop.

Hope it helps.

messages.author: 5e1f5c6d80cc0dca
messages.subject: Re: Working with shapefiles and geom_path
parts:
Hi Manuel
When you use SpatialPolygonsDataFrame is better to use fortify method, so here is my code

require(sp)
require(rgdal)
require(rgeos)
require(maptools)

mymap <- readOGR(dsn = "./carte/", layer = "ZipCodesIntersectingHarrisCounty")

str(mymap)

# or simply fortify (generic S3)
# ? fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame for help
ggmap <- fortify.SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(mymap, region = "NAME")

str(ggmap)

ggplot(ggmap, aes(x = long, y=lat, group =  group)) + geom_polygon(colour = "black", fill = NA)

# if you want to add label

milieu <- function(x) mean(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
centre <- ddply(ggmap, .(id), colwise(centre, .(lat, long)))

ggplot(ggmap, aes(x = long, y=lat, group =  group)) + geom_polygon(colour = "black", fill = NA) + geom_text(data = centre, aes(group = NULL, label = id), size = 2.5, colour = "red")




2011/4/2 Manuel Spínola <mspin...@gmail.com>
